long_biography.plain_text:
Jean-Claude Mimran joined the family enterprise young and worked in Africa alongside his father, Jacques. Jacques had established flour mills and launched a sugar complex in Senegal. After Jacques died in 1975, Jean-Claude and his brothers inherited the group. He became its principal operator, adding mills and plantations while modernising CSS's integrated cane-growing, refining and ethanol operations.

Acquisitions and investments gradually took Groupe Mimran beyond food processing. The group sold its large flour and feed milling businesses to Seaboard in 2018. CSS remained the enduring agribusiness centre, while family capital also moved into mining and energy companies. At CSS, Mimran's chairman-and-chief-executive role sits above a separate director-general responsible for daily management. The plantation, refinery, power facilities and other group interests belong to their respective companies, not to him personally.
